clue.text: Number get a fever that's ill-defined

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five, a number
ague is an old word for a shivering fever such as malaria

explanation.surface: Someone catches a fever whose symptoms nobody can pin down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is often a crossword cue for a Roman numeral: here V, five.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague lacks clear outline or detail, so it is poorly defined.

clue.text: Its lead decreases and it often draws

definitions.text: Its lead decreases and it often draws

parts.words: Its lead decreases and it often draws
parts.note: reads like a team losing its lead and drawing matches, but describes a writing tool whose graphite core wears down as it sketches

explanation.surface: A sports team keeps letting its lead slip and ends up drawing matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the graphite 'lead' wears away with use and the tool is used for drawing.

clue.text: When father came up by himself the rift was obvious

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces are set side by side
in a down clue, coming up means the word for father is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
himself points back to the father, so his word appears again unchanged
a rent is a tear or split, a rift

explanation.surface: A father arrives alone and the family quarrel becomes plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'himself' points back to the father, so the same word is used twice: once turned round by 'came up', once as it stands; 'by' sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible or evident, a synonym of obvious.

clue.text: Earring found on the railway

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery turns up lying on the train tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ring worn to keep a pierced ear open is so called, and the wooden or concrete beams supporting rails on a British line carry the same name.

clue.text: Sound proof of what a performer can do

definitions.text: Sound proof of what a performer can do

parts.words: Sound proof of what a performer can do
parts.note: plays on soundproof: a trial in which a performer's ability is heard and judged

explanation.surface: Insulating a room so you can test what an act is capable of.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trial performance given to show a casting panel one's ability, judged by listening.

clue.text: Miserable? Cheer up!

explanation.surface: Someone looks glum and a friend urges them to brighten up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words, the answer reads as a wish that sorrow should depart, which is what 'Cheer up!' urges.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone means looking sad and wretched; split as a phrase it wishes sadness away, a call to brighten.

clue.text: Drink disrupted pool game

parts.note: water is the most basic drink

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of pool are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's drink spills and spoils a game around the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges POOL into POLO.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a team ball sport played by swimmers in a pool.

clue.text: House party in a rut, perhaps

indicators.note: in signals that the party word sits inside the rearranged letters
perhaps hints that the word rut may be some other arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A household falls into a dull routine of throwing parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests a building, but it is a royal dynasty. 'perhaps' shuffles the rut and 'in' places the party within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I is called a house, as royal families are.

clue.text: Piano music — a duet

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: A piano piece written for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet involves two performers, a couple of people together.

clue.text: Cash exchanged in pure monetary transaction

indicators.note: exchanged means swapped about, so the letters of cash and pure change places

explanation.surface: Ready money changes hands in a straightforward sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' rearranges CASH and PURE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase is a buying of goods for money, a deal involving payment.

clue.text: Arms displayed in a hostile way?

definitions.text: Arms displayed in a hostile way?

parts.words: Arms displayed in a hostile way?
parts.note: suggests weapons brandished, but means hands on hips with elbows out, a confrontational stance

explanation.surface: Weapons brandished threateningly.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes standing with hands on hips and elbows turned out, a posture that often looks defiant.

clue.text: Stick with it!

parts.note: sounds like encouragement to persevere, but literally describes an adhesive you fasten things with

explanation.surface: A coach urges someone not to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive is literally what you fix things together with.

clue.text: The wages of sin-and anger

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the answer is formed out of the letters of sin and anger

explanation.surface: A twist on the Bible's warning that the wages of sin is death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Romans 6:23, 'the wages of sin is death'. 'of' means 'made from': the answer is built out of SIN and ANGER rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money received for work, the same thing as wages.

clue.text: Piping game with Heather!

parts.note: whist is a card game
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A girl named Heather plays a game while a pipe is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant, called LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a shrill sound through pursed lips is a piping noise.

clue.text: Its poor relief, be cautious about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cautious word goes round it

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious

explanation.surface: A warning to be wary about handouts to the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' reads as a possessive but is just a link here; 'about' wraps the cautious word round 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity is help given to people in need, relief for the poor.

clue.text: A bleared version probably isn't

indicators.note: a version is a different form of something, so the letters of a bleared come in another order

explanation.surface: A blurred copy of a document is probably hard to make out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges A BLEARED; and something bleared, blurry, is hardly easy to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurred copy is usually not legible, the very quality the answer names.

clue.text: Pressing time of day?

explanation.surface: Asks when is the best hour for ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' suggests urgency, but here it means making flat or level.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing smooths cloth level, a making-even; and the late part of the day before night has the same name.

clue.text: State carriage?

explanation.surface: A grand ceremonial coach used on official occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State carriage' reads as one ceremonial vehicle, but it is two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an Australian state, and the other is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage named after the queen.

clue.text: Mad liar maybe, and a master of craft

indicators.note: maybe hints that mad liar is one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A crazy fibber who is also a skilled craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges MAD LIAR. 'craft' means ships, not handiwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral commands a fleet, a master of vessels; craft means boats.

clue.text: Said sale was fixed and became aggressive

indicators.note: fixed means rigged or rearranged, so the letters of said sale are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claimed an auction was rigged and lost their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges SAID SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Assailed means attacked violently, behaving aggressively towards someone.

clue.text: Much sought after at the sale

explanation.surface: Bidders at an auction crave a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a great quantity, and items offered at an auction are numbered parcels of the same name.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot a bird

explanation.surface: A hunter readies a gun to bring down a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a gun's hammer ready to fire is one sense, and a male fowl is the other.

clue.text: Spotless tea set put out

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or displaced, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A perfectly clean tea service is laid out on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges SET into STE. 'Spotless' here means morally pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and virtuous, morally unblemished.

clue.text: Construct ring-road on royal command

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the royal Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch decrees that a ring-road be built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Construct' tells the solver to build the answer from the pieces; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is an instruction given with authority, a command.

clue.text: It is involved with a plan that is flexible

indicators.note: involved means mixed up together, so the letters of it and plan are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A scheme that can easily adapt to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges IT and PLAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means bending easily, supple and adaptable.

clue.text: Dilatory sort of hero-worship

indicators.note: sort of hints at a kind of rearrangement of the letters of dilatory

explanation.surface: Lazy, slow admiration of a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges DILATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive admiration, worship of an idol, as of a hero.

clue.text: One loses one's head when in a corner

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the first letter of the word for one

parts.note: single means one, alone

explanation.surface: Someone panics when trapped in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses one's head' suggests panic, but it drops the S from SINGLE. An ingle is a fireside; an inglenook is the chimney corner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireplace, and the snug recess beside it is the chimney corner.

clue.text: See trivia as an odd collection of different things

indicators.note: an odd collection is a jumbled assortment, so the letters of see and trivia are mixed together

explanation.surface: Treat trivia as a strange assortment of miscellaneous items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd collection of' rearranges SEE and TRIVIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Varieties are distinct kinds or types, a range of different sorts.
